questions.question: In a series circuit, if we measure the voltage across each component and add them together, what will this total voltage equal?
options: The total current in the circuit
The voltage of the cell or battery
Zero, because voltage is used up
Twice the voltage of the battery

questions.question: If four 1.5 V electrical cells are connected together in series to make a battery, what is the total voltage of this battery?
options: 0 V

questions.question: What is true about electric charges in the wires of a circuit when the circuit is switched off?
options: There are no electric charges in the wires at all.
Electric charges are present in all the atoms of the wires.
Charges only appear when the battery is connected and turned on.
Charges are only found inside the battery, not in the wires.

questions.question: When a complete circuit is turned on, how do the electrons in the circuit begin to move?
options: They start moving at the same time everywhere in the circuit.
They start moving from the battery first and slowly reach the bulb.
They move only near the switch and then spread out.
They start moving at different times depending on their distance from the battery.

questions.question: How fast do individual electrons actually travel around a typical electric circuit?
options: At the speed of light
At a speed of several metres per second
At a speed of just a few millimetres each second
They do not move at all, they only vibrate in place

questions.question: Why does a faulty filament bulb prevent current from flowing through it?
options: The glass bulb has cracked, letting air in.
The metal base has become demagnetised.
The filament inside is broken, creating a gap.
The bulb has accumulated too much negative charge.

questions.question: If a series circuit stops working due to a single faulty component, how can the circuit be made to work again for the other components?
options: By adding another battery in the opposite direction
By using a wire to bypass the faulty component
By increasing the thickness of all the other wires
By reversing the connections to the ammeter

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a series circuit?
options: A circuit with multiple branching paths for the current to split into.
An electric circuit with one complete loop from one end of a battery to the other.
A circuit that only functions when a voltmeter is connected in series.
A circuit that contains only switches and no other components.

questions.question: How does an ammeter affect the current in the circuit it is measuring?
options: It significantly reduces the current in the circuit.
It doubles the current to make it easier to read.
It measures the current flowing through it without affecting the circuit's current.
It stops the current completely while taking a measurement.

questions.question: Which statement is true about the electric current in a series circuit?
options: The current is highest near the positive terminal of the battery.
The current is lowest after passing through a bulb.
The current is the same everywhere in the circuit.
The current changes depending on how close it is to the switch.

questions.question: What happens to the current in a series circuit when an extra component, such as another bulb, is added?
options: The current decreases only on the side after the new component.
The current changes everywhere in the circuit, on both sides of the component.
The current increases on the side before the component and decreases after it.
The current remains exactly the same everywhere in the circuit.

questions.question: How should a voltmeter be connected to measure the voltage across a component in a circuit?
options: In series, so all current must pass through the voltmeter.
Across the terminals of the component (in parallel).
Connected directly between the positive terminal and the switch only.
Cut into the main wire before the component.

questions.question: What is the correct unit of measurement for voltage (potential difference)?
options: Amps (A)
Ohms (Ω)
Volts (V)
Watts (W)

questions.question: What are the negatively charged particles in atoms called?
options: Protons
Neutrons
Electrons
Nuclei

questions.question: Why is it difficult to charge metals by rubbing them?
options: Metals do not contain any electrical charges.
Electric charge flows through them, preventing charge build-up.
Metals destroy any static charge that touches them.
Rubbing metals causes them to lose all their atoms.
